reason: The support cells and collagen fibers appear to form the skin's supporting tissue.
expectation: They will form a supportive skin layer.

effect: The support cells and fibers formed a layer that can support the rest of the skin.
reaction: The tug panels make the fibers' supporting role clearer.
reason: Cell junctions appear to connect neighboring surface cells into a sheet.
expectation: The junctions will join the surface cells into a layer.

effect: The joined surface cells form a skin patch with slots for protection, support and sensing.
reaction: The named slots make the next steps clear.
reason: The supporting skin layer matches the patch's deep support slot.
expectation: The supporting layer will fit beneath the surface cells.

effect: The supporting layer is fitted beneath the surface, and its vessels supply nearby living cells.
reaction: The inset makes the connection between skin and circulation clearer.
reason: The tough outer layer matches the surface protection slot.
expectation: The outer layer will fit over the surface cells to protect them.

effect: The protective layer is fitted, and the result explains that living cells replace the dead outer cells.
reaction: The distinction between the dead surface and living layers is clear and interesting.
reason: Skin sensory endings match the patch's remaining contact sensing slot.
expectation: The nerve endings will fit into the skin patch so it can sense contact.

effect: The completed skin patch can both protect and sense contact; the next goal is to connect it and the supply network to the arm.
reaction: The cross-section brings the separate layers together clearly.
reason: The skin patch should give the working arm its protective surface and touch sensing.
expectation: The skin will attach to the arm, adding protection and contact sensing.

effect: The skin now covers the arm, and its open vessels await the body supply network.
reaction: The open vessel ends make the next connection clear.
reason: The body supply network matches the arm's open vessel connections and the goal of continuing supplies.
expectation: The network will connect to the arm's vessels and supply its tissues.

effect: The arm is now connected to the body supply network, and the remaining goal is to use contact feedback to hold the glass.
reaction: The new goal gives the assembled systems a concrete task.
reason: The living body model has the sensing and movement systems needed to interact with the glass.
expectation: The hand will use contact feedback to hold the glass steady.

effect: The glass was lifted and steadied using touch feedback and muscle tension, completing the chapter.
reaction: The slipping glass made the role of feedback concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Holding the glass was the most worthwhile action: the slipping and correction sequence connected skin sensation, nerves and muscle work to an everyday task.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the supporting and outer layers was straightforward once the slots were named, though the resulting descriptions added useful biological context.

surprise.text: The explanation that the outermost skin cells are dead while living layers replace them was a useful distinction.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the named slots and item descriptions made the skin assembly understandable.

continue.text: I would try another chapter if it offered another concrete task like steadying the glass. The system connections were interesting, though the assembly choices were often predictable.
